land.text: Sagaing, Thado Minbya's kingdom, which 'declared Sagaing and Pinya constituent countries of Ava'

predecessors.note: Thado Minbya held Sagaing by 30 May 1364 (Ava infobox) and took Pinya in September 1364.
Cliopatria's Ava row starts in 1375 with the same 672 cells as Pinya of 1314; the Toungoo district that broke away from Pinya in 1358 sits inside it as Ava's claim (see notes).

land.text: Ava and Upper Burma, taken by the Confederation of Shan States in March 1527

successors.note: The Ava page keeps the kingdom going to 22 January 1555 under Shan-appointed kings; the Shan States dossier draws the land as Shan from 1527 and the Toungoo conquest of Ava in January 1555 as a loss, so the Ava dossier ends here. Prome (independent since 1482) was the Confederation's ally.

land.text: Toungoo, Kyaukse and Taungdwingyi: the 202 cells that Cliopatria's Toungoo row takes from Ava in 1502

successors.note: Toungoo, de facto independent since 1501, took the Ava heartland only in 1555 (Shan States dossier); listed because its 1502 cells came out of Ava.

capitals.name: Ava (Inwa)
capitals.note: The infobox lists 'Sagaing Pinya Ava' without dates; the text has Thado Minbya 'founded the city of Ava'. Pinya page via the Sagaing dossier: Ava proclaimed 26 February 1365.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1365-1374: Cliopatria's Ava row begins in 1375 although the page has the kingdom founded 26 February 1365 ('by 30 May 1364' Thado Minbya held Sagaing). The outline is the 1375 one (672 cells: Sagaing's 345 and Pinya's 324 cells), which includes the Toungoo district that Pinya lost in 1358: the Mingyi Nyo page shows Toungoo as an Ava governorship (a viceroy, Min Sithu, to 1485) and the Ava page puts Taungoo 'within its fold at the peak of its power', so the claim is kept.

correction.text: Sagaing and Pinya as 'constituent countries of Ava', 1365-1374

keyframe_review.note: 193,597 km2. The Ava page, the Prome page and the Mingyi Nyo page give no area, so no ratio. The outline is Upper Burma from Sagaing to Pyay plus the Toungoo district. The Forty Years' War page has Ava take the Shan states of Kale and Mohnyin and Launggyet in 1404-1406, none of which lies in the outline: they are dated ledger events (Arakan occupation 1406-1408), the Shan lands are not drawn.

192,372 km2: ten cells off the 1375 outline (eight go to Mrauk U along the Arakan Yoma where Min Saw Mon was proclaimed king of Arakan on 18 April 1429; two to the Shan shape in the north-east). Nothing else on the pages changes in 1429-1481; the page says only that 'From the 1420s to early 1480s, Ava regularly faced rebellions in its vassal regions'.

173,537 km2: Prome (63 cells) leaves. 'Mingyi Swa died in 1482' and Thado Minsaw, governor of Tharrawaddy, 'seized Prome and declared himself king' (the infobox dates the kingdom from 1482); Minkhaung II's army 'failed to retake Prome', which 'became an independent kingdom with territories up to Tharrawaddy and Myede'. The Ava page has the break in the 1480s and 1490s.
173,693 km2: the 1482 outline (+2 cells). Nothing dated on the pages in 1487-1501.

114,395 km2: 202 cells (Toungoo, Kyaukse, Yamethin, Taungdwingyi) go to Toungoo. The Mingyi Nyo page has Toungoo 'de facto independent since 1501', Ava's king giving him Kyaukse in 1502, Taungdwingyi under his authority in 1509 and independence announced on 16 October 1510 (the Ava infobox 'Toungoo secession: 16 October 1510'); Cliopatria's 1502 is the de facto year.

114,395 km2, the 1502 outline. The Confederation of Shan States 'sacked Ava' in 1527 (infobox 'Start of Shan period: 14 March 1527'; the Prome page: 'On 25 March 1527, the Confederation forces captured Ava'), so the shape holds for 1526-1527 only; Cliopatria keeps it to 1528 and the Shan row from 1529.

ledger.note: 26 February 1365: Thado Minbya founds the Kingdom of Ava. Infobox 'Kingdom of Ava founded: 26 February 1365'; the text gives 1364 ('The kingdom was founded by Thado Minbya in 1364'); he held Sagaing 'by 30 May 1364'.

region.text: Sagaing and Pinya, with the city of Ava as capital

ledger.note: December 1385: the Forty Years' War begins. 'The war began c. December 1385' when Swa Saw Ke invaded Pegu during its succession struggles; the Hanthawaddy dossier draws the fighting at the approaches to Pegu.

region.text: the approaches to Pegu (Hmawbi, Dagon, Pankyaw)

ledger.note: 1391: the first truce. 'The war was fought during two separate periods: 1385 to 1391, and 1401 to 1424'; Ava 'had to agree to a truce' that ran to 1401.

1401: the war resumes. Razadarit 'invaded Upper Burma in full force with a large flotilla in 1401'; a further truce followed in 1403 and Ava's conquests of 1404-1406 (Kale, Mohnyin, Launggyet) fall inside this phase.

region.text: Pegu and the border with Ava

ledger.note: 29 November 1406: Ava troops overrun Launggyet. 'Ava troops overran Launggyet on 29 November 1406'; Minkhaung I appointed Anawrahta Saw as 'king' of Arakan and Min Saw Mon fled to Bengal. The Forty Years' War page has Ava take 'Launggyet Kingdom (Arakan)' in 1404-1406.

region.text: Launggyet, the Arakanese capital 'overrun' on 29 November 1406

ledger.note: 1408: Pegu drives Ava out of Arakan. 'In 1408, Peguan forces dislodged Avan troops from Arakan'; Arakan was then a Pegu tributary (infobox 1412-1421) until Min Saw Mon's return in 1429.

region.text: Launggyet, the Arakanese capital 'overrun' on 29 November 1406

ledger.note: 1415: Minye Kyawswa conquers the Irrawaddy delta. He 'invaded the Hanthawaddy country in full force in 1414, and conquered the Irrawaddy delta in 1415, forcing Razadarit to flee Pegu for Martaban'.
March 1415: Minye Kyawswa is killed and the delta lost. He 'was killed in battle in March 1415'; after it 'the enthusiasm for war dissipated on both sides'.

Early 1424: the war ends in stalemate. Binnya Ran I made peace by giving his sister Shin Sawbu to Thihathu, and 'Ava forces withdrew in early 1424, ending the four-decade-long war'; the infobox lists 'No long-term changes'.

region.text: Pegu and the border with Ava

ledger.note: 1482: Prome breaks away. Thado Minsaw 'seized Prome and declared himself king' (infobox 1482, the page gives no year in the text); Minkhaung II's army failed to retake it and Ava 'could not send another force for about two decades'. The Ava page has the break in the 1480s and 1490s.

region.text: Prome and the south, 'territories up to Tharrawaddy and Myede' (Prome page): the 63 cells Cliopatria gives to its Prome row in 1482

ledger.note: 1502: Ava's king gives Toungoo's governor Kyaukse. Mingyi Nyo was 'de facto independent since 1501'; 'In 1502, Ava's king gave him Kyaukse, which the page calls the most valuable region in Upper Burma'; Taungdwingyi came under him in 1509 and independence was announced on 16 October 1510. The region is Cliopatria's 202 cells.

region.text: Toungoo, Kyaukse and Taungdwingyi: the 202 cells that Cliopatria's Toungoo row takes from Ava in 1502

ledger.note: March 1527: the Confederation of Shan States takes Ava. 'In 1527, the Confederation of Shan States, led by the state of Mohnyin in alliance with Prome, sacked Ava' (infobox 'Start of Shan period: 14 March 1527'); the Prome page has 25 March 1527 and an earlier sack in March 1525. The Confederation set nominal kings on the Ava throne until the Toungoo conquest of 22 January 1555.

March 1527: the Burmese kingdom of Ava ends. The Ava page runs the kingdom to the Toungoo conquest of 22 January 1555 under Shan-appointed kings (Thohanbwa 1527-1542, Sithu Kyawhtin 1551-1555); the land is drawn as Shan from 1527 (Shan States dossier).

region.text: the whole kingdom, to the Confederation of Shan States

wars.name: Forty Years' War

zones.text: Pegu and the Irrawaddy delta, held 1415

wars.outcome: Stalemate: 'preserving the independence of Hanthawaddy, and effectively ending Ava's efforts to rebuild the erstwhile Pagan Kingdom'; Ava held Kale, Mohnyin and Launggyet in 1404-1406 and the delta in 1415.
wars.note: Two phases, 1385-1391 and 1401-1424, with truces in 1391-1401 and 1403-1408 (the page). Minkhaung I and Razadarit died in 1421-1422.

wars.name: Confederation of Shan States' conquest of Ava
wars.outcome: 'In March 1525, the combined armies of Confederation and Prome sacked the city of Ava' and 'On 25 March 1527, the Confederation forces captured Ava' (Prome page); Ava was 'under intensified Shan raids for the first quarter of the 16th century'.
wars.note: The Ava page has the sack in 1527; the Mingyi Nyo page has Ava besiege Toungoo for a month in April-May 1525 and fail.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a surveyed frontier: the Shan, Arakan Yoma and southern (Prome, Pegu) edges are approximate, and the Toungoo and Shan vassal margins are claims.

sources.title: Kingdom of Ava
sources.note: Identity, 26 February 1365, vassals, Toungoo secession 1510, Shan raids, 1527 and 1555; no area.

sources.title: Prome Kingdom
sources.note: Prome's independence in 1482, its territory, the 1525 and 1527 sacks of Ava.

sources.title: Mingyi Nyo (Mingyinyo)
sources.note: Toungoo de facto independent 1501, Kyaukse 1502, Taungdwingyi 1509, independence 16 October 1510; Toungoo as Ava governorship in 1485.

notes: Cliopatria's row is 1375-1528; the pages put the founding on 26 February 1365 (infobox; the text says 1364) and the Burmese dynasty's fall on 14 March 1527 (infobox) or 25 March 1527 (Prome page). The Ava page and the Wikipedia infobox run the kingdom to 22 January 1555 under Shan-appointed kings; this dossier ends it in March 1527 because the Shan States dossier already draws Ava and Upper Burma as Shan from 1527 (its gain from ava-kingdom) and the Toungoo conquest of 1555 as a loss; if the reviewer prefers one state to 1555, the Shan States gain and this dossier's loss and dissolve both move. The 1365-1374 keyframe uses Cliopatria's 672-cell outline, which still contains the Toungoo district (Pinya lost it in 1358); the sagaing-kingdom dossier suggested the union less Toungoo. Nothing opened dates Toungoo's return to Ava's fold between 1358 and 1485. Not drawn: Ava's 1404 conquest of the Shan states of Kale and Mohnyin and its tributaries Mogaung, Hsipaw and Kalaymyo (the Ava page says 'within its fold at the peak of its power', no dates, outside Cliopatria's outline); the Ming-Mong Mao wars of 1438-1449 and Ava's defeat of Theinni in 1412 (no page opened). Counterparts: hanthawaddy-kingdom, prome-kingdom, first-toungoo-empire, shan-states, sagaing-kingdom, kingdom-of-pinya (all slugs of se-01); 'Launggyet (Arakan)' has no dossier (the Mrauk U kingdom begins in 1429). The Forty Years' War page was opened under the title 'Forty Years' War' (the title with '(Burma)' did not load).
